DESIGN INVARIANTS (do not break these without a paragraph in the methods):
1. max_model_len is 32768 for EVERY reader, including those whose native
window is larger. The serving window is a held constant of the design,
not a per model maximum. Llama 3.1 and Gemma 3 are capped down here.
2. dtype is bfloat16 everywhere. No quantised rung on the axis: compression
perturbation is size dependent and would run parallel to the axis under
test. The W4A16 arm is a separate condition run against the pinned
3. served_name is the reader id, never 'local'. The llm_model column is
what makes rows from two readers distinguishable; a constant string
there makes the whole sweep unanalysable.

readers.notes: Expect the weakest format compliance of the roster. Preflight decides whether this rung is reported as a rank comparison or as a floor.

readers.role: PINNED campaign reader; baseline for every contrast
readers.notes: Identical weights to the campaign run. Any drift between this and the campaign numbers is a bug in the replay, not a finding.

DEFERRED: access request pending with Meta. Kept in the manifest so array indices and the appendix table stay stable; excluded from runs via the READERS variable rather than by deletion. If access has not cleared by the time band B is analysed, substitute the Granite fallback and record the substitution. Native window 131072, capped to 32768 by design. Attribution string 'Built with Llama' required in the artefact README.

readers.role: capacity contrast at band B, in family
readers.notes: Largest KV footprint of the roster at roughly 192 KB per token. This is the only reader where the free KV cache line in the vLLM log needs reading rather than assuming.

GATED. (1) The chat template has NO system role and folds system content into the first user turn; the frozen reader prompt is flat text with no system role, so this does not arise on the measured path. (2) The checkpoint is multimodal. vLLM 0.22.1 parses --limit-mm-per-prompt as JSON, so the key=value form is rejected; --language-model-only is used instead. It runs the model text-only (all modality limits set to 0) but still loads the vision weights: 22.52 GiB at load, leaving 32.71 GiB of KV cache, 364,297 tokens, 11.12x concurrency at the 32768 window. (3) Release postdates LongMemEval, so its C0 leakage number is load bearing.

fallbacks._comment: Substitutes, only if the primary cannot be served or staged. Record any substitution in the methods, since it changes the family set.

llama-3.1-8b-instruct.notes: Ungated, so no access queue. Dense 8B, independent corpus from both Qwen and Gemma, does the same band A family contrast. Take this if the Meta request has not cleared by the time band B is analysed, rather than letting the roster block the chapter.

gemma-3-12b-it.notes: Only if the container's vLLM cannot serve Gemma 3. Text only, no template surprises, but 24B sits above band B so the capacity match to Qwen2.5-14B is looser. Fits one GCD at roughly 47 GB with about 16 GB left for KV; verify the free KV line before trusting it.

excluded._comment: Recorded so the appendix can say why, rather than leaving the reader to wonder.
excluded.microsoft/phi-4: Native context 16384, below the 32768 serving window. Would have required either a shorter window at one point of the design or context extension at one point, both of which break the held constant.
excluded.allenai/OLMo-2-1124-13B-Instruct: Native context 4096 with longer inputs relying on RoPE extrapolation. Same reason as above, more severely.
excluded.inclusionAI/Ling-lite: Mixture of experts, 16.8B total and 2.75B active, so parameter count is not a scalar capacity variable. Named in future work as a sparsity probe rather than a rung.
excluded.openai/gpt-oss-20b: Mixture of experts, native MXFP4, reasoning mode. Three confounds stacked on the capacity axis.
excluded.Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct: Qwen License rather than Apache 2.0, and requires TP=4 for roughly ten times the wall clock of band A, in exchange for a rung that adds little to a rank invariance claim.
